deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. There are no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a continuous passage of an official expert opinion (Gutachten) addressed to the 'hohes Curatorium' of Göttingen University. Its subject is a proposal, apparently from General Baeyer and transmitted by a 'gesandtschaftliche Note', to join Hanover to a Central European arc measurement (Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung, early 1860s).

The argument runs as follows:

(1) The previous page concluded that the Hanoverian triangulation (Gauss's survey) is complete and is the most important foundation for determining the figure of the Earth. This page continues the sentence: the authors accept what the Rescript says about the second foundation, the astronomical determinations of latitude and longitude.

(2) They nevertheless hold that this astronomical foundation can and should be extended. The reason is that recent times have brought entirely new means, 'in dem electrischen Telegraphen' (interlinear addition). These were unknown before and open the way to the finest longitude determinations.

(3) The existing astronomical foundation consists of two parts:
- first, Gauss's determination of the latitude difference between Göttingen and Altona (the zenith-sector work of 1827 at the ends of the Gauss arc);
- second, the longitude differences between the principal European observatories, obtained by chronometer expeditions under Schumacher's direction.

(4) For the higher scientific purpose, following ideas Gauss had already developed, it would be very important to have astronomical latitude and longitude differences of the highest accuracy. Ideally these would cover all principal triangulation points, or at least a larger number of points in the country. This is implicitly about comparing astronomical with geodetic coordinates, i.e. deflections of the vertical and the departure of the geoid from the ellipsoid.

The next page goes on to request two things: a telegraph line from the observatory to the Göttingen telegraph station, and a telegraphic registering apparatus (Hansen/Ausfeld, Gotha, 200 Thaler).

What the page contains in the way of method is only the standard idea of telegraphic longitude determination. In modern terms, Δλ = (local time difference of the same signal) = (θ_A − θ_B), with clocks compared by electric signal instead of transported chronometers. This is stated qualitatively, not computed.

results.what: Advocacy of telegraphic longitude determination to supplement chronometer-expedition longitudes and Gauss's Göttingen–Altona latitude difference, for use in determining the figure of the Earth
results.modern_name: Telegraphic method of longitude determination; astro-geodetic determination of vertical deflections
results.usually_credited_to: Telegraphic longitudes: Arago's suggestion, then the US Coast Survey under Bache and Walker (from the 1840s); Central European arc measurement: J. J. Baeyer (1861–62); the geodetic ideas: Gauss

deep.surprise_reason: This is administrative text from a committee report on geodetic and astronomical infrastructure (Baeyer's Gradmessung proposal). The page has no mathematics. Its scientific content, using the telegraph for longitudes and Gauss's ideas on combining astronomical and geodetic positions, was standard by the early 1860s. The authorship of the wording is likely collegial (e.g. with W. Weber), and Riemann may be the scribe or co-author. Riemann's involvement in such Göttingen faculty reports is of minor biographical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Line 6: the interlinear mark above 'daß die' reads like 'da' or 'dr'. It is probably a revision turning 'daß' into 'da', so the sentence becomes '...wünschenswerth sei, da die neueste Zeit...' after the deletion of 'mit besonderer Rücksicht darauf'. The machine transcription's 'da[?]' is plausible.
Line 6: the interlinear insertion 'in dem electrischen Telegraphen' is written in a lighter (reddish) ink above 'ganz neue Mittel'. It is correctly placed as an insertion after 'die neueste Zeit'.

The first word of the second paragraph, transcribed 'einzige[?]', is doubtful. The sentence goes on to list two foundations ('erstens… zweitens…'), so a reading like 'bisherige', 'wichtigste' or similar is more plausible than 'einzige'. Re-check against the image.
'erstens' and 'zweitens' are underlined in the manuscript.
Line 4–5: 'sogar' appears struck through. This is consistent with the transcription's deletion mark.
The marginal '70' at right is the folio number, not part of the text.
A long pencil stroke runs vertically through the middle of the second paragraph. It is probably a cancellation or 'copied' mark and is not reflected in the transcription.
